comment: Frame 019, printed p. 13: the cities of the third clime continued, entries 148-164: Ṭaḥā, then ten places of Egypt, al-Qays, Iqnā, Ahnās, al-Bahnasā, Qamin, Dalāṣ, al-Fayyūm, Manf, Qaṣr Miṣr and ʿAyn Shams, for which the table gives two longitudes, the second after the word «اخرى»; then Qūnā, al-Qulzum on the sea, a city, Madyan, al-Jār and the city of the Prophet. Two lines of the editor's footnotes, with one word of a third.

observations: The table goes on from frame 018 without a heading: the cities of the third clime, entries 148-164. For entries 149-158 the table has a further pair of columns, ruled like the others, between the names and the longitudes: it holds a first longitude, degrees and minutes, then the word «اخرى» stands between the columns, and the longitude columns hold the second; the latitude follows as usual. Entries 148 and 159-164 have one longitude, and their names stand over the further columns; transcribed so, the name spanning them. Entries 148-158 have no numbers of Suhrāb; entries 159-164 have [١٢٤]-[١٢٩]. Entries 148-158 and 160 and 163 are printed without the word «مدينة»; entry 161 is the word «مدينة» alone.
L02: the editor's note a, at the first «اخرى», says that the word نسخة is to be supplied: «نسخة اخرى», another copy. The note mark stands only at L02; the word recurs without it in L03-L11.

L02-L04, L07: the minutes of the second longitude are printed as a zero sign between angle brackets, «⟨ō⟩», the editor's sign for what he supplies; his notes b, c, d and f say that the minutes are missing in the manuscript.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: ٮح (L02, the first longitude; L03, the second), the tooth without its dot; ٮو (L13, the degrees of the longitude), the tooth without its dot; ٮه (L07, the minutes of the latitude; L08, the minutes of the second longitude), a tooth joined to a final ه; ں (L10, the minutes of the second longitude), the bowl of a final ن without its dot. With their dots: نز (L01), نح (L02, L04, L05), ند (L06-L11), نه (L12), the ن with its dot; ن (L10, L11, the minutes of the first longitude); كز (L01, L02) and نز (L01), the ز with its dot; يه (L01, L09, L14), the ي with its two dots. The isolated ه, 5 (L06, the minutes of both longitudes), is a small round ring.

L03, L07, L12: the degrees of the latitude are printed كر, with ر, and L14: the degrees of the longitude, ٮر; in these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII). Transcribed ر as printed.

L14: the degrees of the longitude, ٮر: a tooth without a dot joined to a ر, the two strokes forming a notch at the top, where the isolated ر of the font is a plain curved stroke (frame 021, L09, where the ر alone stands for 7); the neighbouring entries have نه, ٮو, سا, سد and سه. Transcribed ٮر.
L08: «الفيّوم», with a shadda over the ي. L02: two small specks stand on the line after «القيس»; they are not transcribed.
The isolated ك of the minutes (L07, the first longitude; L13, the latitude; L15-L17, the longitude) is printed with the small inner stroke of the letter.
The page number «— ١٣ —» stands at the foot, centred.
